translation: For one who sets bones (正骨), one must have a clear mind and skillful hands. Only after knowing the condition of the illness and moreover being good at using the manual techniques will treatment naturally be effective. Truly, the hand is originally a body of flesh and blood; the subtlety of its turning and application can, through one's own flexing and extending, high and low, fast and slow, light and heavy, opening and closing, reach the patient's congealed and stagnant qi and blood (氣血), swollen and painful skin and flesh, contracted and broken sinews and bones, and the suffering and desire of the emotions. Compared with using instruments to engage in restraint, the difference is very great.
